title: What is the initial information architecture of the application shell?
statement: The first slice must choose which views exist: project overview, stage view, artifact tracker, assertion/evidence view, or some subset. The choice determines what the vertical slice has to render and what it may defer.
notes: The vertical slice as scoped needs a stage view at minimum, because it displays the current stage and one stage document. `app/server.mjs` already renders an assertion/evidence view against the same substrate, so that view has a working reference implementation and is the cheapest to reach parity on — which is an argument about ORDER, not about what the first slice must contain. ⚠️ ANSWERED LAST, AND NOT BY RESEARCH (pm, 2026-08-24). This is principally a PRODUCT decision, not a research question: no source settles which views a planning tool should open with. It is sequenced fifth so it is decided under the constraints the other four establish rather than ahead of them — a deployment mode (QST-0017), a component bound on what a document may execute (QST-0018), a server/client module boundary (QST-0020) and a runtime lifecycle (QST-0021) each remove options from the information architecture before it is chosen. Choosing the IA first would mean designing views against constraints nobody had established, and then rediscovering them. ⚠️ PROPOSED 2026-08-27, AFTER THE OTHER FOUR CLOSED, and no search credit was spent because this question said not to: no source settles which views a planning tool opens with. What the sequencing bought is not evidence but ELIMINATION — four decisions now remove options that would otherwise have been discovered by building them. ⚠️ WHAT THE CONSTRAINTS ACTUALLY REMOVE (the first two are logical consequences of the decisions, not measurements, and are flagged as such). (a) DEC-0022 makes every content change and every reconnection a FULL PAGE RELOAD. So no view may hold state the reload would destroy: open panels, active tabs, scroll-restored lists and client-side filters are out of the first slice unless they are encoded in the URL. This is the sharpest constraint and it is the one that would have been discovered last. (b) DEC-0019 blocks prefetching as an accepted cost, so every navigation is a round trip with no warm-up. That argues for FEWER, DENSER views rather than many thin ones a user would page through — an inference from the accepted cost, not something measured. (c) DEC-0020 compiles stage documents per request, at a cost that is explicitly unmeasured. A view that rendered several documents at once would multiply an unknown, so: at most ONE stage document per view until that cost is measured. (d) DEC-0021 exposes only what the shell needs through `app/server/*`, and holds back locking and process-spawning modules for individual review. Read-only views are cheap; the review-status write goes through the locking path and is the one capability the first slice must actually get reviewed and exposed. (e) DEC-0022's truthful-count rule binds every summary surface: a tracker or dashboard that reports totals must report only what it rendered. ⚠️ PROPOSAL — TWO VIEWS, both URL-addressable, both server-rendered, no client state. `/` — the project view: the derived current stage (REQ-0016), all nine stages with their gate state, artifact counts under the truthful-count rule, and lint findings surfaced rather than re-judged (#47). `/stage/[stageId]` — the stage view: that stage's document as restricted MDX (REQ-0017), its exit criteria with recorded attestations, and the review-status action through the typed write path (REQ-0019). That is the whole first slice. It satisfies REQ-0016 through REQ-0019 and nothing else, and both views survive an arbitrary reload because neither holds state. ⚠️ DEFERRED, WITH REASONS RATHER THAN SILENCE. The artifact tracker and the assertion/evidence view are deferred even though the SKELETON ALREADY IMPLEMENTS THE LATTER — DEC-0017 keeps `app/server.mjs` as the verified substrate reference until the new shell reaches parity, so that view has a working home today and reaching parity on it is roadmap step 5, not step 4. Authoring, search, graph and cross-stage navigation are out: none is required by REQ-0016..0019, and each would add state the reload contract forbids or a surface the count rule would then have to cover. ⚠️ WHAT WOULD CHANGE THIS. If per-request MDX compilation is measured to be expensive (DEC-0020's third obligation), the stage view is where it hurts, and the fallback is that decision's own second alternative — plain markdown — rather than a different information architecture. And if reload-on-change proves too coarse in use, the answer is a finer change signal, not client-held state; the reload contract is what makes the missed-change class of defect impossible. ⚠️ STILL A PM DECISION (#34). Recorded as a proposal; the question stays unanswered until it is approved. ⚠️ AND IT DOES NOT SETTLE CACHE COMPONENTS: nothing above depends on that flag, which is the property DEC-0019 was chosen to preserve.
